question: Resolve the $0.82bn of top-50 Schedule I grants (FY2023-24) to EINs in neither Pub 78 nor the EO BMF with no church/government/subordinate/LLC label, plus $0.64bn of blank or placeholder EIN lines: fuzzy-match names and states against the BMF and Pub 78 to estimate how much is sponsor EIN misreporting versus unrecognised grantees
conclusion_affected: Size of the EIN-validation / grantee-verification problem a DAF entrant's grant rail must solve; whether sponsors' public filings show weak recipient-identity controls
rationale: The exact-name check found only $0.05bn of likely EIN errors, but cases such as Heartland Alliance ($16.6m), LA Clippers Foundation ($15.5m) and a 'Fidelity Charitable' line under a revoked wrong EIN suggest that most unexplained absence is misreported EINs. Only public IRS files are needed

question: Date the revocation hits: for the 568 lines ($21.6m) to EINs revoked before or during the grant year and absent from Pub 78/BMF today, and the 136 lines ($4.4m) whose BMF ruling postdates the sponsor's year-end, use prior monthly Pub 78/BMF snapshots (IRS/archived 2022-2024 copies, if available publicly) to test whether the recipient was listed at grant time, the Rev. Proc. 2018-32 reliance point
conclusion_affected: Whether sponsor due-diligence controls are effective (reliance on published IRS data) and how much value a real-time revocation monitor adds for sponsors
rationale: 85% of revocation-hit dollars were posted before the sponsor's year-end, but Schedule I has no grant dates and the IRS lists are current snapshots. The list's reinstatement field is blank for most re-recognised organisations ($53.1m of the $74.8m are back in the lists)

question: Screen Schedule F (foreign grants) and the expenditure-responsibility population: for the top-50 sponsors FY2023-24, parse Schedule F Part II grant totals by region and list Schedule I lines to Pub 78 PF/SONFI and non-501(c)(3) recipients ($81.7m and $29.6m), separating DAF from community foundations' discretionary grants where the return allows
conclusion_affected: How much DAF grantmaking needs equivalency determination or expenditure-responsibility workflows (a product requirement for entrants), and the international share of DAF grants
rationale: Schedule I Part II is domestic only, so foreign grantees were not screened. Columbus Foundation's $43.6m to the Huntington Foundation (PF) and community foundations' grants to 501(c)(4)s show expenditure-responsibility cases concentrated at community foundations
